rules: External solvers, search and AI submit bytes, not authority. A success flag or checker URL cannot create evidence.
Certificate and subject bytes are snapshotted, bounded, re-hashed and decoded canonically before invoking a host-registered checker.
The certificate must bind the exact caller-selected subject. The checker must return its configured claim class for that same subject.
The Core proof adapter matches the actual public interface and sends the exact proof admissions to pinned configured kernel providers.
Unsupported certificates, missing checkers, disagreement, resource failure and infrastructure failure do not become semantic acceptance.
Accepted certificates produce only a live session-owned scoped validation handle. Serializable receipts are audit data.
A checked theorem interface is not automatically a global compiler-preservation claim; that relation-to-theorem mapping needs a separate checked contract.
remaining: solver-specific proof-term or compact-certificate translators/checkers as those formats are admitted
actual kernel-provider replay and adversarial certificate campaigns
formally checked global relation-to-theorem mappings and verifier refinement
